$source: LandBank Desktop Web design tokens (colors_and_type.css), sampled 1:1 from the Claude-designed Requirements Studio app

accent.$use: logo + restricted UI (channel/CALL-CENTRE pill) only — never a general CTA colour

surfaces.$note: surfaceInset (added Phase 5 item 4) reuses this brand's own canvas value rather than inventing a new tone: the shesha default brand's surfaceInset (#F0F2F5) happens to equal ITS OWN canvas-adjacent divider tone, and RS's canvas (#f0f2f5) is the same literal — the closest existing RS analogue for a muted/recessed chip fill (card-with-header-strip's count badge, rail-panel's count badge). This was a dangling $palette.surfaces.surfaceInset reference before this fix.

chrome.$note: detailRailWidth/navTileWidth/metricTileWidth/chartMinHeight/formColMax (added Phase 5 item 4) are pure structural/layout metrics, not colour or brand decisions -- they are the shesha default's own values, reused as-is because no RS-specific measurement for a record-detail rail column / nav tile / metric tile / chart surface / wizard form-column exists anywhere in this brand's source material, and there is no reason layout-budget pixel widths should differ by brand absent one. This brand's OWN railWidth (56, collapsed sidebar rail) and recordBarHeight (96) are unrelated, differently-scoped chrome concepts that were already correctly not confused with these before this fix -- see resolve-role.test.mjs and roles.styles.json's detail-rail/nav-tile/metric-tile/chart-surface/wizard-shell roles.

roles.$note: divider/bodyInk/mutedText/progressAccent (added Phase 5 item 4): this brand's own palette already carried the backing values (lines.divider, ink.primary, ink.soft, brand.primary) -- only the role-map entry exposing them was missing, an omission rather than a genuine brand decision. bodyInk deliberately targets the same path as bodyText (matching the shesha default's own bodyInk/bodyText pair); progressAccent matches Ant Design's own convention of a Progress bar defaulting to the theme's primary/interactive colour.
